title: fix(agents): gate ask_user by channel capability
body:
Fixes #161445
Fixes #167469
Related: #111470

## What Problem This Solves

`ask_user` can start a question on a channel that cannot reliably deliver or complete it: WhatsApp DMs fail with `REPLY_DISPATCH_DELIVERY_ERROR`, and Mattermost turns can wait on an unseen question.

## User Impact

Eligible primary sessions retain structured questions on WebChat/native OpenClaw clients, Discord, Slack, and Telegram. On Mattermost, iMessage, Signal, WhatsApp, and undeclared channels, the agent asks in ordinary plain text. Explicit tool denial still wins. Approval reactions remain unchanged.

Peter's product decision is to gate built-in `ask_user` by declared native question input and retire bundled question-reaction fallbacks. This addresses the built-in `ask_user` failure reported in #167469 by omitting the tool from Mattermost. The separate native Claude `AskUserQuestion` path also mentioned in that report bypasses this catalog and remains outside this fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conversation capability owner resolves `questionInputMode` once from the authoritative inbound channel. Coding tools, Gateway catalogs, and skill dispatch carry that fact into registration; a supported fallback provider cannot enable questions on an unsupported inbound surface.

Bundled question-reaction adapters and obsolete tests are removed. The reaction SDK factory and members shipped in stable v2026.9.8 remain unchanged for third-party compatibility, with no removal date. The only additive SDK contract is optional `agentPrompt.questionInputMode: "buttons"`, documented on the existing channel adapter; no new named export is needed.

Docs name the supported surfaces and explain plain-text questions elsewhere. A nearby CI fixture defect is also fixed: the final iMessage self-chat test left fake timers active during asynchronous database teardown. One file-level cleanup hook now replaces two incomplete per-suite hooks, without changing assertions or timeouts. No schema, retention, or new deferred side effect is introduced.

Original fix by @jacobtomlinson; maintainer cleanup reconciles current main, completes direct-catalog propagation, preserves shipped SDK contracts, and updates docs and regression coverage.

## Evidence

Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38851063599) completed successfully on attempt 2 for `c6443b005a44f4679d6257f2b5213ad3d586c217`, after merging main `d372cddb9f`: 59 jobs passed and 27 were skipped. The previously failing Slack shard and aggregate gate passed on the latest attempt. PR CI is the test and typecheck gate per maintainer policy. Local tests, local typechecks, negative controls, live Gateway proof, and remote leases were intentionally skipped.

- `ask_user channel catalogs` in `channel-catalog.contract.test.ts`: ten cases using real bundled declarations through the existing public-artifact loader; supported/unsupported channels, authoritative inbound selection, and explicit denial.
- `gates ask_user in the $messageProvider catalog (deny: $deny)`: three real Gateway catalog cases.
- `gates ask_user on the inbound $message.surface surface (deny: $deny)`: four real skill-dispatch cases, including unknown inbound surface with a supported provider.
- Retained supported-flow coverage includes `publishes the prompt through Bot API and completes after the answer`, cached-question authority, and approval-reaction/partial-delivery tests.

Changed-file core `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check` passed. The temporary lint config preserved every applicable core rule and omitted only an unmatched UI-only Solid override whose dependency was absent from the supplied install. Docs sanity passed on all ten changed pages. Full isolated Codex autoreview and each subsequent repair review were scoped-clean through P2.

Prior-head CI exposed and guided three repairs: use the public-artifact loader in an existing collected contract suite; retain SDK exports without increasing the deprecated-export ratchet; restore real timers before iMessage teardown. No baseline, assertion, or timeout was weakened. Current-head CI passed all 18 tests in `channel-catalog.contract.test.ts`, including the ten-case matrix, in a 52.50s shard (76% transformation, 16% tests). Production/test typechecks, lint, docs, baseline, boundary, and the previously failing iMessage shard passed. Earlier CI also ran the retained Telegram round-trip in 8.330s and passed the four new skill-dispatch cases; those timings are prior-head evidence.

ClawSweeper's direct-catalog and shipped-SDK findings are addressed. Its Mattermost support concern is superseded by the product decision above. Live-proof-only requests are superseded by the maintainer proof policy.

Exact numstat against merged main: production +50/−415 (−365), tests +129/−458 (−329), docs +75/−35 (+40); total +254/−908 (−654) across 42 files. The 17 new catalog cases add no timers, sleeps, network calls, or test-only production seams.

Earlier CI failure: attempt 1's [job 116812813808](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38851063599/job/116812813808), `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1-1`, failed `extensions/slack/src/monitor/provider.auth-test-token.test.ts` / `does not use a user-token identity as the bot mention target` with `StateDatabaseAccessError: ... is undergoing offline maintenance; retry when it finishes.` The coordinator diagnosed a test-state flake; the PR's only Slack change is the declarative `questionInputMode: "buttons"`. The failed job was rerun, and the same exact-head shard passed on attempt 2. This is a successful retry, not a claim that the flake itself was repaired. The current-head security-sensitive review status is successful; no approval command was posted.

Feishu #111470 is related: its undeclared surface is gated, but this PR does not claim to repair Feishu choice-card delivery.
